A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting and content relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original human ratings for 300 generated videos, metric comparisons, external-benchmark evaluations, and model ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds a 23-action evaluation, further controlled experiments, and additional MLLM prompting results.

M1.justification: The main encoder, feature fusion, losses, and scoring rules remain unchanged. Appendix E.6 adds a limited training variant that supplements temporally corrupted real-video negatives with CogVideoX-generated hard negatives; it is presented as an experiment, without replacing the default procedure.

E1.justification: Section 5.5 adds training and evaluation across 23 actions, extending the original ten with thirteen classes including Hammering, PlayingGuitar, RockClimbingIndoor, and Surfing. The original benchmark, renamed TAG-Bench-v0, remains. Kinetics-700 and VBench-2.0 coverage already existed in v1.

E2.justification: Appendix G.2 expands the in-context-learning comparison from Qwen3-VL to include GPT-5 and Gemini-2.5-Pro with demonstrations. The original main benchmark comparator set is retained completely in v3 Table 12; its shorter main Table 1 does not represent baseline removal.

E3.justification: Additional experiments introduce matched prompt comparisons using 30 initial frames, retraining with 3–100 samples per class, fusion controls, and metric-selected in-context demonstrations. The original evaluation retains its 80/20 split, 90-epoch training budget, 32-frame windows, Spearman correlation metric, and human-rating protocol.

E4.justification: Appendices E.4–E.6 and E.9–E.10 add outlier case studies, detailed-generation-prompt testing, generated-negative ablation, four-way feature-fusion comparison, and training-sample sensitivity. G.2 expands the in-context-learning analysis. Existing loss, feature, temporal-distortion, window-length, attention, and Kinetics analyses remain; the Kinetics experiment moves from the main text.

E5.justification: v3 Section 5.2 newly reports p < 0.05 and 95% bootstrap confidence intervals over the 300 videos: [0.52, 0.63] for action consistency and [0.59, 0.68] for temporal coherence. Existing human-rating reliability analyses remain. No additional training-run or seed counts are reported.

E6.justification: Original benchmark scores are retained. New 23-action results are 0.59/0.56 for the proposed metrics versus GPT-5's 0.46/0.39. Additional results cover fusion, sample counts, generated negatives, and a 55% enhanced-prompt win ratio. Table 14 adds action-consistency correlations of 0.47 for GPT-5 and 0.34 for Gemini-2.5-Pro with demonstrations. These concern additional settings.

T1.justification: The feature-fusion, training-loss, scoring, and rater-filtering equations are retained. The added experimental explanations introduce no substantive theoretical assumptions, mathematical revisions, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the learned human-action manifold, human-rated benchmark, two evaluation metrics, and stronger alignment with human judgments. The abstract retains its greater-than-68% improvement claim. Additional experiments support these existing claims without redefining the core contribution.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly acknowledges unreliable pose/HMR features under occlusion and frames the ten-class study as a proof of concept. New analyses interpret data efficiency, fusion choices, and semantic versus anatomical failures. G.2 qualifies the earlier prompting discussion by recognizing modest, example-sensitive benefits from metric-selected demonstrations.

D1.justification: v3 discloses the filtered per-class sample range of 42–137 and describes additional fusion and demonstration-selection procedures. Core implementation settings and code access remain unchanged. Conversely, its shortened Qwen demonstration description omits v1's explicit two-clip count and assurance that those clips were outside the evaluation set.

R1.justification: v3 adds the CogVideoX paper as reference 68 for the new demonstration experiment. The related-work discussion and principal positioning against existing video metrics remain substantially unchanged; most other reference differences are numbering or bibliographic formatting.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order remain recognizable. Changes include the TAG-Bench-v0 terminology, localized prose shortening, simplified subsection hierarchy, relocation of the Kinetics analysis, and reorganization of Appendix E and the in-context-learning discussion.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from two columns to a single-column layout. Figures 1–2 are rearranged or redrawn; the full baseline table moves to the appendix with an abridged main version. New outlier figures and sample-size/ICL tables are added. v1's per-video Qwen score-distribution figure is removed, while its aggregate comparison remains.

improvement.justification: v3 provides a modest net gain through broader action coverage, additional design and data-efficiency checks, bootstrap intervals, and clearer limitations. Benefits are tempered by sparse documentation of the expanded study, removal of the Qwen distribution plot, and an inaccurate 'top-3' summary that includes Gemini-2.5-Pro despite omitted Qwen3 scoring higher on both axes.
